page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.8xlarge is a storage-dense cloud server built on x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. The instance is equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. System memory totals 128 GB, providing an allocation of 4 GB RAM per virtual core. Network performance is supported by a baseline bandwidth rate of 20 Gbps.

The primary hardware differentiator for the ecs.d1ne.8xlarge is its bundled local storage array, offering 94,489 GB of local HDD capacity directly attached to the instance. This massive storage density provides strong qualitative cost efficiency per gigabyte when evaluated against standard cloud storage options, allowing users to host extremely large datasets locally without incurring separate cloud disk attachment overheads.

The primary tradeoff of this instance architecture relates to disk media characteristics. Because the local storage relies on mechanical HDDs rather than solid-state or NVMe drives, access times and random I/O operations per second are limited relative to modern flash-based instances. Consequently, the ecs.d1ne.8xlarge is optimized for workloads requiring bulk capacity and sequential throughput rather than low-latency random reads. Suitable deployment scenarios include big data analytics platforms, distributed file system storage nodes, centralized log aggregation, data warehousing, and long-term archival storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.8xlarge is a storage-dense instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors clocked at 2.5 GHz, paired with 128 GB of memory. Its primary differentiator is the bundled local storage capacity of 94,489 GB delivered via HDD drives, supported by a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Operating on x86_64 architecture under KVM, this server maintains a balanced general-purpose memory ratio of 4 GB RAM per vCPU alongside high-density physical storage. While mechanical HDD storage incurs higher access latencies compared to NVMe SSD alternatives, the large volume of local disk space delivers favorable qualitative cost efficiency for throughput-bound storage requirements. The hardware profile exhibits a clear tradeoff between raw random IOPS performance and sheer local storage capacity per compute node. This server configuration is best suited for big data processing, log analytics, distributed file system nodes, archival infrastructure, and large-scale data warehousing.
